blurb_title: The pod could not find the HSM. The test pod next to it could.
blurb_1: This guide abolishes the unseal ritual from Nº 1: afterwards the root key is encrypted with an RSA key that never leaves a Nitrokey HSM 2. The stick hangs off the Kubernetes worker, the pod gets the pcscd socket as a hostPath, a custom image brings OpenBao's HSM build and OpenSC. For readers without HSM experience, Part I explains what seal, token, SO PIN and DKEK mean – and why the last question comes before the first key.
blurb_2: The way there: the official image cannot do PKCS#11; pcsc-lite 2.4 in the container speaks 4:5, pcscd 2.0.3 on the host only 4:4; OpenSC 0.26 names the token differently than 0.23; a read -p in zsh yields an empty Secret. Then unseal -migrate, three times – and a pod that comes up without a key. Two drafts to close: one HSM for all pods, and the plugin path of OpenBao 2.7.
